{"url": "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all%3AHow+do+computational+theories+of+autobiographical+memory+distinguish+between+stored+experiential+data+and+a+persistent+sense+of+identity%3F&max_results=4", "scope": "paper abstracts; preprints, peer-review status not verified", "excerpt": "title: Observation of the rare $B^0_s\toμ^+μ^-$ decay from the combined analysis of CMS and LHCb data
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4413v2
published: 2014-11-17T10:10:25Z
summary: A joint measurement is presented of the branching fractions $B^0_s\toμ^+μ^-$ and $B^0\toμ^+μ^-$ in proton-proton collisions at the LHC by the CMS and LHCb experiments. The data samples were collected in 2011 at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV, and in 2012 at 8 TeV. The combined analysis produces the first observation of the $B^0_s\toμ^+μ^-$ decay, with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far. Furthermore, evidence for the $B^0\toμ^+μ^-$ decay is obtained with a statistical significance of three standard deviations. The branching fraction measurements are statistically compatible with SM predictions and impose stringent constraints on several theories beyond the SM.

title: Expected Performance of the ATLAS Experiment - Detector, Trigger and Physics
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/0901.0512v4
published: 2008-12-28T14:58:59Z
summary: A detailed study is presented of the expected performance of the ATLAS detector. The reconstruction of tracks, leptons, photons, missing energy and jets is investigated, together with the performance of b-tagging and the trigger. The physics potential for a variety of interesting physics processes, within the Standard Model and beyond, is examined. The study comprises a series of notes based on simulations of the detector and physics processes, with particular emphasis given to the data expected from the first years of operation of the LHC at CERN.

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=Can+simulative+reasoning+frameworks+effectively+detect+reasoning+blind+spots+without+relying+on+pre-defined+evaluation+datasets%3F&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7304238\", \"title\": [\"Logical Equivalence, Metacognitive Interference, and Scoring Blind Spots in Inductive Reasoning Tests: On the Structural Invalidity of IQ Scores as a Measure of Reasoning Ability\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The test items used in IQ testing to measure fluid reasoning-whether number series or figural matrix reasoning-all rely on the same inductive reasoning structure: \\\"given finite samples, infer a rule, predict the next term.\\\" This paper identifies three structural problems with such items: (1) Logical equivalence: given any finite sequence or matrix, there often exist multiple generative rules that are computationally equivalent in their outputs, yet the test scores solely on output, making it impossible to distinguish the quality of reasoning paths; (2) Metacognitive interference: high-metacognitive test-takers automatically engage an \\\"auditing procedure\\\" (questioning the premise of the item, identifying multiple interpretations), which consumes working memory resources and induces response delays, resulting in systematic time-pressure penalties; (3) Skeptical disposition and deference to authority presuppositions: the standardized testing procedure implicitly demands that test-takers not question the items themselves, not question the testing institution, and not question the system which claims that intelligence can be measured by a single score. Test-takers with a habitual skeptical disposition automatically initiate the auditing procedure, consuming additional cognitive resources and thereby being systematically penalized in performance. Furthermore, practice effects allow test-takers to compress \\\"reasoning\\\" into \\\"pattern matching,\\\" thereby bypassing the auditing procedure and significantly improving scores-this further demonstrates that when practice becomes normative, what the test measures is no longer fluid reasoning but crystallized pattern recognition.
